scope: BP038 client NMT_Login field2 borrowed-FString serializer ownership/lifetime

source_snapshot_observed.finding: The fixed field2 return-site hook builds an owned std::wstring, passes only a 16-byte RawNativeFString view to the pinned serializer, then clears the owned string after the synchronous call. The original native field2 is not replaced or released by this hook.

The signed Grant and encoded Steam ticket stay staged across reliable retransmits and are cleared only at terminal/cancel/failure boundaries; native_grant_injected is a staging/hook completion bit, not a serializer ownership proof.

BuildUrlWithGrantAndSteamTicket creates an owned terminal-NUL std::wstring and does not adopt or mutate caller-owned FString storage; this is a transport/storage guarantee, not proof that the engine serializer does not retain the borrowed view.

The API comment requires synchronous save-only borrowing and retains the Grant until the native transition reaches a terminal state; this contract still requires runtime ownership evidence before treating the fixed callsite as proven.

evidence.finding: At serializer RVA 0x0189D2DE the save branch consumes the source FString shape and calls the archive writer synchronously; the captured branch has no source FString Data/Num/Max write. Its temporary encoding release is at 0x0189D41C and is distinct from caller-owned field2 storage.

The save branch calls a virtual archive operation at [archive-vtable+0x10] and later a writer operation at [archive-vtable+0x150]. The static listing does not establish whether either callee stores a source data pointer or schedules asynchronous work.

The fixed client sequence calls the serializer at 0x03484F35 (field2 return site 0x03484F3A), then the identity serializer, then field4 at 0x03484F51 (return site 0x03484F5D), followed by the send/dispatch call at 0x03484F79.

After the send path returns, the locked caller releases field4 through the known allocator call and reaches the field2 release after return site 0x03484FBD; this is the original caller field lifecycle, not proof about the hook-owned temporary buffer.

static_callsite.static_conclusion: The callsite is compatible with a synchronous borrowed view, but static control flow alone does not prove that the archive writer never retains the data pointer or that the fixed serializer has no deferred consumer.

proves: The historical local-PVE client reached the pinned outbound serializer sequence.
The observed original field2 object retained the same pointer/Num/Max shape across the serializer call.
A matching field2 storage release was observed after the known caller send path.
does_not_prove: The observed field2 was the Payload-created borrowed temporary; the historical run used the unmodified original field.
The archive writer did not retain or asynchronously read the field2 data pointer.
No alternate allocator/destructor path released the pointer.
A strict online Grant reached server PreLogin or passed Backend/Steam admission.

proves: Server field2 shape flowed into the fixed URL/options helper chain and then both observed PreLogin boundaries.
The server-side owned field2 storage was released at the observed final release boundary.
does_not_prove: Client field2 and server field2 values correspond byte-for-byte.
The server helper cannot retain a pointer after its call returns.
Platform possession, signed Grant acceptance, or native connection admission.

current_component_run_boundary.observation: The component run records native_grant_staged/native_grant_injected status but has no co-located nmt serializer or allocator observer artifact. Those status bits show the Payload hook reached its own completion marker; they do not establish serializer enter/leave ownership, absence of deferred reads, or absence of a temporary-buffer free.

source_constraints.fact: Config.MinPlayersToStart is 1 only for explicit PvE and 2 for online authority.

The match-start gate counts ConnectedPlayerControllers and opens its role-selection countdown only when NumPlayersJoined reaches Config.MinPlayersToStart; the role-selection flow remains upstream of pawn/playable readiness.

current_component_playable_boundary.interpretation: The one-real-Steam-client plus synthetic-seat component run closed Native/Backend admission through CONNECTED but did not reach the product role-selection/pawn gate. This is consistent with the fixed online minimum of two joined players and the observed single initial late-join queue; it is a separate playable-matrix limitation, not evidence that serializer injection retained or freed a borrowed FString incorrectly. A second real Steam session is required for full playable acceptance; do not lower MinPlayersToStart or use a synthetic seat as strict online PASS.

minimum_next_observation.classification: OFFLINE_ABI_ONLY when using local-PVE; component-only evidence when attached to the one-real-Steam harness
attach_order: Discover the exact owned client PID after the game process is created and verify its image hash before the client sends NMT_Login.
Load a frozen read-only sidecar before the client-ready/Grant marker is emitted; attach to the exact authority PID separately with the server observer if server-side relation is needed.
Keep the existing ordinary game dispatcher untouched; this is Frida observation only and must not use ManualDispatch or alter callback ownership.
End at the owned process exit or a bounded timeout, then record no strict PASS unless the normal Backend/native receipt chain independently closes.
required_read_only_events: serializer.enter for field2 at return RVA 0x03484F3A: call ordinal, thread id, return RVA, archive shape, FString object/data pointer hashes, Num/Max, readability; never read data bytes.
serializer.leave: RAX return pointer hash, same object/data pointer/Num/Max shape immediately after return, and same call ordinal.

archive writer enter/leave: resolve the fixed archive vtable slot used by serializer save control flow ([archive-vtable+0x10] and the later writer slot), record only archive/data pointer hashes, byte count, thread and duration; no buffer reads.
fixed caller checkpoints at 0x03484F3A, 0x03484F79, 0x03484F86, 0x03484FAF and 0x03484FBD to order serializer return, send, archive cleanup, and original field releases against the per-call record.

allocator/destructor observations for the hook-owned temporary data pointer through the known FMemory free target plus process allocator free exports (HeapFree/RtlFreeHeap or the actual loaded CRT target); record exact pointer-hash matches and order only.

bounded post-return pointer-access observation, if available through a read-only MemoryAccessMonitor/watchpoint, to detect a read/write of the temporary data or 16-byte view after the serializer returned; record operation/address hash only, never bytes.
minimal_sidecar_changes: Do not modify the existing frozen observer in place. Clone it under a run-specific immutable name and record the clone SHA.
Add a monotonic call_id and per-thread active-call map; the current observer loses correlation at the generic free hook and cannot distinguish field2 calls after pointer reuse.
Add an archive writer hook resolved from the archive vtable after the first matching field2 enter; filter by archive pointer and active call_id.
Add fixed caller return-site probes and a bounded pointer-lifetime map covering the hook-owned data pointer separately from the original field2 data pointer.
Add exact allocator path labels and a release-generation counter; a generic FMemory::Free hit alone is insufficient to claim no alternate C++/CRT free path.
Hash all pointer values with a per-run salt before writing evidence; keep Num/Max/byte counts and RVAs only.
safe_run_constraints: No Interceptor return-value replacement, memory write, call to a game function, or ManualDispatch.
No FString data, URL, Grant, Steam ticket, player ID, JWT, or callback payload bytes in the output.
Verify fixed image hash and only observe the exact owned PID; do not broad-scan or kill unrelated processes.
Use a bounded 120-second window, preserve raw sidecar output privately, and publish only a redacted summary plus input/output hashes.
A negative/inconclusive observation keeps native client grant injection unverified; it cannot be converted to readiness by setting a boolean.
acceptance_requirements: For at least three matching field2 serializer calls, the injected temporary data pointer is observed at enter and writer enter/leave, with no post-return read/write or retained pointer event during the bounded lifetime window.
The temporary pointer has one observed allocator release after the synchronous call, while the original caller field2 release remains separately ordered at 0x03484FBD.
No archive/serializer callback is observed after the temporary release; any unknown target, missing allocator coverage, pointer reuse, or thread handoff is PARTIAL/BLOCKED, not PASS.

This ABI result remains separate from the strict online proof: signed Grant, native Steam possession, Reserve -> NativeAdmit -> Confirm, local readiness, and release still require their own exact scoped evidence.

final_assessment.next_action: Run the frozen read-only client/server sidecar concurrently with the next owned component harness, or explicitly record the missing serializer/allocator attachment as NOT_RUN. Do not infer ownership safety from native_grant_injected=true.

dynamic_sidecar_runs.reason: Pinned PreLogin byte gate failed; online authority bootstrap was refused before a client could reach NMT_Login. Sidecar loaded on exact-hash authority but observed no serializer or allocator events.
